title: Python SDK: decorator-based streaming handler API and event contracts
creator: Lina Cheng
description: Problem: current Python SDK streaming surface relies on low-level callback or async-iterator patterns that are powerful but awkward for common cases: combining lightweight per-event transforms, retry semantics, backpressure signaling, and deterministic teardown. Goals: provide a high-level, composable decorator-based API that expresses event contracts (Message/Token/Done/Error), surface backpressure controls, and interoperates with existing async-iterator usage. Non-goals: removing async-iterator support; implementing server-side streaming changes.
design_summary:
Proposal: introduce @stream_handler decorator and a small event contract module (redwood.sdk.streaming.events) with typed event names. Handlers can be sync or async and receive typed event objects. Support middleware composition for retries and metrics. Key ergonomics: - Default safe contract (Message, Delta, Token, Error, Done) - Automatic buffering with explicit flush/backpressure signals from handler return values - Built-in retry middleware with idempotency hints - Fallback hook to non-streaming path when streaming is unavailable Example API (illustrative):

from redwood.sdk import Client
from redwood.sdk.streaming import stream_handler, events, RetryMiddleware

client = Client()

@stream_handler(event_types=(events.Message, events.Done), buffer_size=8)
async def chat_handler(evt):
    # evt.type == events.Message | events.Done | events.Error
    if evt.type is events.Message:
        # evt.content is incremental chunk or token
        await process_chunk(evt.content)
    elif evt.type is events.Done:
        await finalize()

# Compose middleware when creating client/route
client.add_stream_middleware(RetryMiddleware(max_attempts=3, backoff=0.6))

Compatibility: the decorator returns an invocation token that can be used with client.stream_invoke(handler, request). The existing client.stream() returning async iterator remains supported; internally the decorator system adapts an iterator to the handler and vice versa.
acceptance_criteria: Add stream_handler decorator and events contract module to python SDK
Provide Retry and Backpressure middleware primitives and documentation
Unit tests covering ordering guarantees, drop/flush semantics, and retry hooks
Integration test against local devserver demonstrating fallback to non-streaming path
Docs + 1 migration example (callback -> decorator) in SDK guide
decisions: Keep async-iterator API for advanced users; decorator is opt-in ergonomic layer.
Backpressure API will use explicit handler return signals (e.g., StreamAction.FLUSH / StreamAction.WAIT) rather than raising to control flow.
Retry middleware will be responsible for idempotency hints; handler authors can opt out via decorator flag.
No breaking changes to wire protocol; all changes are client-side ergonomics.
implementation_notes: Tasks: (1) event contract enums and lightweight classes (Message, Token, Delta, Error, Done); (2) decorator plumbing that adapts handler to existing stream router; (3) middleware chain (metrics, retries, backpressure); (4) tests + docs. Performance: avoid allocating per-token objects in hot path; use pooled lightweight Event views for streaming hot paths. Observability: emit metrics streaming_latency_ms, streaming_retry_attempts, streaming_backpressure_waits, streaming_event_drops.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: new ergonomics may mask ordering semantics and cause subtle reordering when handlers do I/O. Mitigation: document strict ordering guarantees (handler called sequentially on events for a given stream) and provide an option to switch to 'parallel handler' mode. Risk: backpressure semantics could deadlock user code that awaits on external resources. Mitigation: default buffer_size conservative (8) and provide clear guidance + examples.
migration_plan: Phase 1: add decorator as beta feature behind opt-in flag in client (Client(streaming_api='decorator-beta')). Phase 2: collect telemetry for adoption and bug signals for 4 weeks. Phase 3: promote to default with opt-out flag. Provide two-line migration examples in the SDK guide and a codemod script that converts a common callback pattern to decorator usage.
testing_plan: Unit: event order, buffer behavior, backpressure signals, retry hooks. Integration: run against local devserver with artificial latency and injected stream errors to validate retries and fallback. Property tests: randomized event sequences to validate handler state invariants. E2E: example app in examples/chat/ using decorator and CI job that runs against a nightly runtime image.
metrics_and_monitoring: Add metrics: streaming_latency_ms (p50/p95), streaming_on_stream_error_count, streaming_retry_count, streaming_backpressure_wait_count, streaming_fallback_count. Dashboards: per-route streaming stability and per-version adoption. Alerts: increased fallback_count or retry_count by >200% over baseline -> page oncall SRE.
docs_and_examples: Docs: new 'Streaming Handlers' section in python SDK guide with three examples: simple echo handler, streaming summarizer with backpressure flush, and retry-resilient compose example. Example code will be in /examples/python/streaming_decorator/ and linked from the release notes.

2026-03-09 Diego Martinez: Added RetryMiddleware prototype and integration test that simulates transient 503s; handler-level idempotency flag works as expected. Filed PR for review. CI flake on property-based tests under heavy concurrency; reducing concurrency in tests for stability.
